main_body: A blue-grey sci-fi wall face with panel sections, an orange stripe, orange shelf bars and a vent panel, all drawn flat on one vertical plane, with a lower base band
top_band: none - the column starts with a 1-row light outline and a dark blue wall face; no horizontal top surface is visible. The orange band (row 5-6) is a stripe on the wall face, not a top.
evidence: The kind is terrain (wall face), which is a vertical surface drawn face-on. The scan shows an outline row, a dark wall field, an orange stripe, panels and a base band, with no lighter horizontal top surface above a front face. Panels are slightly inset, but the whole piece is a front elevation of a wall face. A wall-face autotile of this kind is expected to be flat, so this is front-on by design; the terrain kind carries no top-band requirement beyond reading as a wall.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 14 distinct colours against 68 for the timber reference and 33 for the stone reference. Its median of 9 colours per tile is below the timber reference's 26 and the stone reference's 13. Its 7% flat-fill coverage is higher than the references' 0%: the panel interiors and the dark lower band are large flat areas of one colour. Its outlines are tinted dark blue (0% near-neutral), so the material-tone outline is fine. Shading has about 4 steps (light edge, mid blue, dark blue, deep navy) against 5-6 in the references, and surface texture is limited to a few highlight dots and bolt squares. It reads as thinner and flatter than the references, so it fails.
